nodes.content: Develop an open-world visual recognizer that distinguishes novel classes from domain shifts while learning new classes without forgetting.
requirements: Achieve ≥80% novel-class recall at ≤5% false rejection of domain-shifted known classes.
After ten class additions, retain ≥95% initial known-class accuracy and achieve ≥70% added-class accuracy.

nodes.content: Calibrate frozen CLIP prototype novelty scores on shifted known images; learn new classes with replay-trained adapters and logit distillation.
Can shift-calibrated CLIP prototypes prevent weather-induced false novelty without masking unseen classes?
On WeatherShift-10, shift-calibrated prototypes will achieve ≥80% novel recall at ≤5% shifted-known false rejection, outperforming global CLIP thresholds.
Calibrate on shifted-known validation images; compare WeatherShift-10 novel recall against global CLIP thresholds at 5% false rejection.
Evaluate calibrated prototypes against global CLIP thresholds on held-out WeatherShift-10 weather, reporting novel recall at 5% shifted-known false rejection.
On held-out WeatherShift-10, calibrated prototypes achieved 83% novel recall at 5% shifted-known false rejection versus global CLIP’s 68%.
Adopt shift-calibrated prototypes for novelty detection; their 83% recall meets the target at 5% shifted-known false rejection.
Integrate the adopted novelty detector with replay-trained adapters; run ten sequential class additions, measuring known-class retention and added-class accuracy.
WeatherShift-10 evaluation bundle containing calibrated-prototype checkpoints, ten adapter snapshots, and per-addition known-class retention and added-class accuracy logs.
Which replay-buffer size and distillation weight preserve known-class accuracy after ten additions without suppressing added-class learning?
Sweep 20/50 replay exemplars per class and distillation weights 0.5/1.0 across ten WeatherShift-10 additions; measure retention and added-class accuracy.
On WeatherShift-10, the best replay/distillation setting retained 92% of initial known-class accuracy after ten additions, despite 74% added-class accuracy.
Retain shift-calibrated novelty detection; replace shared adapters with class-specific low-rank modules and frozen known-class logits to reduce forgetting.
Train class-specific low-rank modules with frozen known logits through ten WeatherShift-10 additions; test retention, added accuracy, and novelty.
Use n10’s prototype checkpoint and baseline logs to train ten class-specific LoRA modules with frozen known logits and compare retention.
WeatherShift-10 bundle containing ten class-specific LoRA checkpoints, a frozen known-class classifier, and per-addition retention comparisons against n10.
Evaluate n17 checkpoints on WeatherShift-10: ten-addition retention versus n10, added-class accuracy, and novel recall at 5% shifted-known false rejection.
WeatherShift-10: LoRA yielded 96% initial-known retention versus 92% baseline, 72% added-class accuracy, and 82% novel recall at 5% shifted-known rejection.
On unseen CameraShift-10 sensor shifts, does frozen calibration still hold shifted-known false rejection to ≤5% after ten LoRA additions?
After ten LoRA additions, WeatherShift-10-calibrated thresholds will yield >5% shifted-known false rejection on unseen CameraShift-10.
Test n17’s ten-addition checkpoint on unseen CameraShift-10 without recalibration; measure shifted-known false rejection and novel-class recall.
On unseen CameraShift-10, shifted-known false rejection was 4.8%, refuting the predicted breach; novel-class recall fell to 76%.
Bootstrap CameraShift-10 sensor groups for 95% confidence bounds on shifted-known false rejection after ten LoRA additions without recalibration.
Sensor-balanced CameraShift-10 bootstrap estimated 6.1% shifted-known false rejection (95% CI 5.2–7.0%), despite the sample-weighted 4.8%.
Defer CameraShift-10 deployment: 4.8% sample-weighted rejection masks 6.1% sensor-balanced rejection, while novel recall reaches only 76%.
Augment CLIP prototypes with simulated sensor artifacts and calibrate sensor-balanced novelty margins, retaining frozen-logit class-specific LoRA modules.
Simulate Bayer noise and compression; calibrate sensor-balanced margins, then test CameraShift-10 recall, rejection, known retention, and added accuracy.
Generate Bayer-noise and JPEG-quality-30 known-class variants; recompute CLIP prototypes and fit equal-artifact-weight novelty margins without CameraShift-10 data.
SensorCal-v1 checkpoint containing artifact-augmented CLIP prototypes, equal-artifact-weight novelty margins, and the unchanged ten-addition LoRA modules.
Evaluate SensorCal-v1 on held-out CameraShift-10 using fixed margins; report sensor-balanced rejection, novel recall, and ten-addition retention and added-class accuracy.
CameraShift-10: SensorCal-v1 reduced sensor-balanced rejection to 4.7%, but novel recall reached only 78%; retention was 96%, added-class accuracy 72%.
Does Bayer-noise or JPEG augmentation cause SensorCal-v1’s missed novel classes on CameraShift-10?
Ablate Bayer-noise and JPEG augmentation in SensorCal-v1; compare CameraShift-10 novel recall and sensor-balanced rejection using simulation-calibrated margins.
CameraShift-10: Bayer-only calibration achieved 82% novel recall at 4.9% sensor-balanced rejection; JPEG-only achieved 75% at 4.8%.
JPEG augmentation broadens known-class similarity neighborhoods, causing at least 5-point lower CameraShift-10 novel recall than Bayer-only calibration.
Compare paired CameraShift-10 novel-to-known cosine margins under Bayer-only versus JPEG-only prototypes; bootstrap recall gaps and inspect JPEG-only missed detections.
JPEG-only prototypes raised median novel-to-known cosine similarity by 0.04 versus Bayer-only; novel recall fell seven points (95% CI 5–9).
Sweep JPEG quality 30/60/90 atop Bayer augmentation; measure known-prototype neighborhood occupancy and CameraShift-10 novel recall at 5% rejection.
With margins recalibrated to 5% rejection, Bayer+JPEG quality 30/60/90 retained 81–83% recall versus Bayer-only’s 82%; neighborhood occupancy rose ≤1%.
Adopt Bayer+JPEG with recalibrated margins; JPEG-only loses seven recall points, but combined variants retain 81–83%.
Bayer coverage, not JPEG-broadened neighborhoods, drives errors; adding Bayer to JPEG-only prototypes raises held-out-sensor recall ≥5 points at ≤5% rejection.
Add Bayer variants to JPEG-only prototypes, recalibrate both to 5% rejection, and compare held-out-sensor recall and prototype coverage.
Simulation-calibrate matched JPEG-only and JPEG+Bayer prototypes; compare CameraShift-10 sensor coverage and novel recall at 5% rejection.
CameraShift-10: adding Bayer increased sensor coverage from 78% to 89% and novel recall from 75% to 82% at 5% rejection.
Leave one Bayer mosaic pattern out of prototype augmentation; measure CameraShift-10 sensor-wise coverage and novel recall at 5% rejection.
On held-out RGGB sensors, JPEG-only recall was 74%; Bayer augmentation without RGGB reached 76% at 5% rejection despite 88% coverage.
Include all tested Bayer patterns, but defer unrepresented-sensor deployment: full coverage reached 82% recall; withheld RGGB reached only 76%.
Mosaic-pattern match, not aggregate sensor coverage, determines recall: including RGGB augmentation restores ≥80% RGGB novel recall at ≤5% rejection.
On RGGB CameraShift-10, compare JPEG-only prototypes with matched and mismatched Bayer variants, measuring novel recall at 5% sensor-balanced rejection.
On RGGB CameraShift-10, matched Bayer raised recall from JPEG-only’s 74% to 82%; mismatched Bayer reached 76%, all at 5% rejection.
Repeat matched-versus-mismatched Bayer augmentation on BGGR sensors with equal prototype counts; measure novel recall at 5% rejection.
On BGGR CameraShift-10, matched Bayer yielded 78% novel recall versus mismatched Bayer’s 82%, with equal prototype counts at 5% rejection.
Use diverse Bayer prototypes with sensor-wise validation: matched RGGB reaches 82% recall, but unmatched RGGB and matched BGGR miss 80%.
Learn sensor-conditioned Bayer-prototype weights using held-out proxy classes; calibrate worst-sensor rejection while retaining frozen-logit LoRA.
Train sensor-conditioned weights on disjoint proxy classes; calibrate worst-sensor rejection, then test CameraShift-10 recall, retention, and added-class accuracy.
Initialize from n10’s prototypes; train sensor-conditioned Bayer weights on disjoint proxy classes, retain n17’s LoRA, and calibrate worst-sensor rejection.
SensorGate-v1 checkpoint with proxy-trained Bayer weighting, worst-sensor novelty thresholds, frozen known logits, and ten class-specific LoRA modules.
Evaluate SensorGate-v1 on held-out CameraShift-10: per-sensor rejection and novel recall, plus ten-addition initial-known retention and added-class accuracy.
CameraShift-10: SensorGate-v1 achieved 83% novel recall (worst sensor 80%), maximum sensor rejection 4.9%, 96% retention, and 72% added-class accuracy.
Adopt SensorGate-v1 for CameraShift-10: it meets novelty, worst-sensor rejection, known-class retention, and added-class accuracy targets.
Extend SensorGate-v1 with image-derived sensor embeddings and uncertainty-gated prototype mixing for unseen cameras, preserving frozen-logit LoRA.
Can image-derived sensor embeddings select reliable prototypes for unseen cameras without increasing shifted-known rejection above 5%?
On UnseenCam-6, uncertainty-gated sensor embeddings achieve ≥80% novel recall with ≤5% shifted-known rejection per camera.
Using n58, train image-derived, uncertainty-gated sensor embeddings on proxy cameras; test UnseenCam-6 per-camera novel recall and shifted-known rejection.
UnseenCam-6: gated embeddings achieved 84% pooled novel recall, 80% minimum per-camera recall, and 4.8% maximum shifted-known rejection.
Adopt uncertainty-gated embeddings for unseen-camera novelty detection; minimum recall reached 80% with maximum shifted-known rejection 4.8%.
Integrate adopted embeddings with ten-addition LoRA; evaluate UnseenCam-6 novelty recall, per-camera rejection, known-class retention, and added-class accuracy.
Combine n17’s ten-addition LoRA modules with n58’s sensor gate and adopted embeddings; measure UnseenCam-6 retention, added accuracy, recall, and rejection.
UnseenCam-6 integration bundle with gated sensor embeddings, ten LoRA checkpoints, and per-camera recall, rejection, retention, and added-accuracy logs.
Audit n70 on a held-out UnseenCam-6 split after ten additions, measuring per-camera recall, rejection, known-class retention, and added-class accuracy.
After ten additions, UnseenCam-6 achieved 82% novel recall, 4.9% maximum camera rejection, 95.5% known-class retention, and 71% added-class accuracy.
Advance separately validated WeatherShift-10, CameraShift-10, and UnseenCam-6 configurations; each meets novelty and ten-addition accuracy targets.
